PullRequest.Title: sessions: improve workspace preselection and telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Make explicit workspace handoffs survive setup and late provider/view readiness, require acknowledgement from the target picker, and cancel stale requests when newer user intent wins. Offer Retry and Choose Workspace for failed explicit handoffs.
- Suggest the invoking editor's folder for generic command and keyboard openings, using the active-file root in multi-root workspaces. Preserve existing sessions, restored drafts, input, attachments, No workspace, and explicit user choices.
- Include folders from recent `.code-workspace` files, preserving history ordering, deduplication, filtering, and removal behavior. Bound file reads and handle unavailable providers, malformed files, remote paths, cancellation, and timeouts.
- Extend `agents/firstTimeWindowOpen` with argument categories, selection provenance, readiness, handoff timing, and initial-versus-emission snapshots. Add `agents/workspaceSelectionOutcome` to measure default retention and first successful request, with focused regression tests and updated accessibility help.

## Why

The opening source alone does not distinguish an existing-session handoff from a workspace request, and the legacy preselection flag cannot explain late defaults or their origin. This improves workspace selection without overriding user intent and adds diagnostics to evaluate usefulness rather than only the percentage of populated pickers.

## Reviewer notes

- Retain the existing event and legacy fields. New telemetry uses categorical state, booleans, and bounded timings/counts; no workspace identifiers or request content are emitted.
- Workspace handoffs retry for up to 15 seconds after setup/restoration preparation. History expansion reads at most 10 workspace files, limited to 1 MiB each, with a shared five-second timeout.
- Outcome observation applies to first-time eligible initial openings without an existing-session argument and ends at the first successful request, shutdown, or three minutes. A timeout without a request is not proof of permanent abandonment.

## Validation

- `npm run precommit`: passed for all 42 changed files.
- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- Focused unit tests: **288 passing across all 14 affected test files**, using `scripts\test.bat` with `--force-device-scale-factor=1 --reporter dot`.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npm run gulp -- compile-client`: blocked by the same three pre-existing Copilot SDK typing errors involving `clientInfo` in `CopilotClientOptions` and `autoTier` in `CapiSessionOptions`. Those source files are unchanged by this PR.
- Real desktop sign-in/startup flow has not been manually exercised.

### Suggested manual checks

1. Open Agents from single-folder and multi-root editor windows. Verify fresh composers receive the appropriate folder while existing sessions and drafts remain intact.
2. Complete initial setup with a pending explicit handoff, and verify delayed provider readiness applies it. Selecting another workspace or navigating to a new session should cancel the older request.
3. Open with recent multi-root workspace history; verify folder selection, ordering, and that removed derived folders remain removed after restart.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The trigger, call path, fan-out bound, and non-propagating extension-provider cancellation are directly visible in repository code. The exact number and latency of provider registrations vary by installation, which affects severity but not the repeated-I/O mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-process IPC calls plus filesystem/extension-host reads and JSON buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each filesystem-provider registration or removal restarts one `getRecentlyOpened()` IPC and fans out to as many as 10 workspace-file reads (up to 1 MiB each), so cost grows as O(provider events × recent workspace files).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated I/O/IPC and restarted five-second loads delay recent-workspace availability and add startup I/O/CPU pressure in the Agents window.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, filesystem-provider registrations did not refresh session workspace history, and VS Code history refreshes did not parse `.code-workspace` files.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added unfiltered global registration listener invokes `_refreshVSCodeRecentWorkspaces()` for every added or removed scheme; each refresh cancels the prior scan, performs `getRecentlyOpened()`, and may launch up to 10 `readFile`/parse operations.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `this._register(this.fileService.onDidChangeFileSystemProviderRegistrations(() => this._refreshVSCodeRecentWorkspaces()));` newly binds every provider add/remove event to the full history scan introduced below.
Findings.Title: Filter filesystem-provider events before restarting history expansion
Findings.Impact: When built-in or extension filesystem providers register after the fresh composer is created, unrelated schemes repeatedly restart recent-workspace loading. A window with 10 recent `.code-workspace` entries can issue 10 reads per event and keep the picker history in `loading` until registrations settle; extension-backed `readFile` calls cannot be canceled at the provider RPC, so superseded scans can continue consuming I/O.
Findings.Evidence: `FileService.registerProvider` fires this global event for every scheme and for unregisters. `_refreshVSCodeRecentWorkspaces` crosses the desktop workspaces proxy via `getRecentlyOpened()` and `Promise.all`s up to `MAX_RECENT_WORKSPACE_FILES` calls to `_readWorkspaceFolders`; `_readWorkspaceFolders` calls `fileService.readFile`. The extension-host `RemoteFileSystemProvider.readFile` forwards `$readFile` without a cancellation token, so disposing a superseded refresh does not necessarily stop the underlying boundary operation. This repository also registers several unrelated Agents filesystem schemes at `WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored`, making the trigger realistic during window startup.
Findings.Recommendation: Track schemes for recent workspace files that could not be read and refresh only on an `added` event for one of those schemes (or otherwise filter by relevant config-path schemes); ignore unrelated registrations/removals and coalesce matching events so only one scan can proceed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an Agents window into a fresh composer with an inferred or explicit workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing main-process `vscode:selectAgentsFolder` IPC must arrive, setup/restoration must reach the required phase, and the target view must acknowledge the workspace. Explicit handoffs also await `openNewSession`; inferred defaults await initial restore. The 100 ms retry loop is on this path but is bounded to 15 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the workspace/session opening intent from main process to the Agents renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC already carried folder, session, and source; the diff adds the default-classification argument.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The renderer cannot apply the handoff before this message arrives.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active handoff per window; newer intents cancel the prior one. The retry loop performs at most about 150 synchronous attempts, each scanning the small registered sessions-provider set until one resolves the single folder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one handoff is retained by `MutableDisposable`; cancellation and navigation/version observers supersede older work. No concurrent retry loops survive replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-open cache is used. Provider resolution is recomputed during retries; the target picker preserves existing user/session choices. Warm readiness usually resolves on the first attempt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cancellation ownership, retry bound, and synchronous provider resolution are explicit in the changed code and provider implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count and readiness latency vary, but built-in `resolveWorkspace` implementations inspected are synchronous URI/object work, so the bounded polling was not reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new retry work is bounded, single-flight, and does not itself cross a subprocess/filesystem/network boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and expand VS Code recent folders and `.code-workspace` history for the workspace picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agents-owned recents are available synchronously, but VS Code recents and automatic selection remain in `loading` until `getRecentlyOpened`, all selected workspace-file reads, parsing, filtering, and publication finish. The picker can render meanwhile, but late automatic preselection/history waits for the latest refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch recently opened workspaces through the desktop workspaces proxy/main-process history service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call initially and one more for every recent-history or filesystem-provider registration event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial/recent-history lookup existed, but filesystem-provider changes did not place this IPC on a new repeated path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each restart postpones publication of VS Code history and late automatic selection until the newest scan completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse recent `.code-workspace` files, potentially through extension-host or remote providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 10 concurrent reads per refresh, each capped at 1 MiB; multiplied by provider registration/removal events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, recent workspace files were not opened or parsed by this service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads are joined before history is published; slow reads hold the load in progress up to the shared five-second timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 10 recent workspace files per refresh, each capped at 1 MiB; total work is multiplied by every global filesystem-provider add/remove event because the new listener restarts the full scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each refresh launches up to 10 reads through `Promise.all`. A new refresh disposes the prior logical operation, but unbuffered/extension-backed provider `readFile` calls do not receive the cancellation token and can continue underneath; no debounce or scheme filter coalesces events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed history is cached only in `_vsCodeRecentFolders` until the next refresh. There is no parsed-file cache, and every provider event resets load state and rereads all selected workspace files, including for unrelated schemes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the global event source, unfiltered listener, IPC lookup, ten-read fan-out, and lack of provider-level cancellation for extension-backed unbuffered reads are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of late provider registrations and whether recent workspace files are local, remote, or extension-backed varies by installation; this lowers severity but not confidence in repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-I/O regression: unrelated provider events restart the full bounded fan-out and can delay history readiness.

Scenarios.Scenario: Observe first-window workspace selection and first successful request for telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observation is passive and off the request critical path: composer state is sampled by an autorun, send options are correlated in a `WeakMap`, and one outcome event is emitted on first successful request, shutdown, or the three-minute timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per eligible initial Agents-window opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This outcome event did not exist; the existing first-window event remains separately bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry emission occurs after a successful send or on timer/shutdown and is not awaited by the user workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial eligible window, one bounded three-minute observer, and weak entries only for sends attempted during that interval.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No spawned parallel boundary work; the first terminal event wins and clears all observers/timers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A single default snapshot and weak request correlations are retained only until emission; no unbounded key retention or negative cache exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disposal, timer, weak correlation, and one-shot emission are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry transport batching is outside the inspected code, but the call count is strictly one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; allocation, retention, and telemetry fan-out are bounded and off the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate among new composers, existing sessions, quick chats, and voice-created sessions while a handoff may be pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Explicit navigation records a new observable token/version and immediately cancels a pending handoff observer; normal navigation then follows the existing session-opening path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One small object/observable update per explicit navigation or active-session change; work scales with user navigation frequency, not frame/render frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Navigation versions and request tokens serialize intent by invalidating older handoffs; no queue or burst of boundary operations is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only the latest navigation object and integer versions are retained. Composer event subscriptions switch with the active composer and unsubscribe from old event signals when observers move.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing observable subscription teardown and all changed navigation call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; per-action allocation is constant and small.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 44 changed files and all diff pages. One medium repeated-I/O finding was submitted for unfiltered filesystem-provider events restarting the new workspace-history IPC/read fan-out. Other changed polling, telemetry, navigation, and observable lifecycles are bounded or off critical paths.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
